The Lamplighter

By Wren Okafor · March 3, 2024 · 2 min read

He climbs the evening one rung at a time,
a wick of patience in his weathered hand;
the street goes gold behind him, rhyme by rhyme,
as if the dark were something he had planned.

And no one thanks him. No one ever will.
The windows fill with faces turned away.
He lights the last one at the top of the hill
and walks back down into the end of day.

This poem first appeared in our Winter issue.
